<!-- Lecture b -->

## [15b] Reviewing Claims

::: {.callout-note}
## Coming soon

This lecture is planned but not yet written. The outline below shows what it is
intended to cover.
:::

::: {.topics}
- Checking a reported test for internal consistency (statistic, *df*, and *p* must agree)
- Recovering effect sizes and confidence intervals from what was reported
- Detecting impossible summary statistics from means, *SD*s, and sample sizes
- Reading a results section for what is *missing* rather than what is wrong
- Writing a statistical review that is specific and actionable
:::

This is the reviewing half of the chapter, and it is deliberately a *statistical*
skill rather than a methodological one: everything above can be checked from the
numbers a paper already reports, without access to the data.
